minutes.headline: Cemetery Commission voted to pull its sale-of-lots warrant article and look to capital planning for expansion and road work.
minutes.summary: The commission heard the DPW director's winter update, then voted to pull its warrant article for a transfer from the sale of lots account. It also voted to accept that capital planning would fund the North Cemetery expansion and the North Cemetery road repairs, though no amounts were settled and the roads item did not appear on the latest capital list. A resident criticized the commission during public comment, and the meeting adjourned with the next meeting set for March 27th.

public_comment.topic: Announcement that bridge work over the brook starts next Friday, with the road closed and detours until the end of April.
Thanks to the town for posting the notice on Facebook and for the state open meeting law webinar.

Criticised the commission for seeking capital planning money without a plan, listed past spending he called wasteful, said he had submitted a warrant article to rein in its funds, and proposed moving the commission under the Conservation Commission.

votes.motion: Approve the minutes of the January 9, 2025 meeting.
Pull the warrant article for the additional transfer from the sale of lots account.
Move forward on the North Cemetery expansion, with capital planning to fund an amount still to be determined.
Accept that capital planning will move forward with the North Cemetery road network repairs.

budget_items.topic: Capital items and sale of lots transfer
budget_items.what_was_said: The chair reviewed a capital item for North Cemetery expansion, a road network repair item, and a transfer from the sale of lots account, after speaking with the town manager and finance director.
The chair gave the account balance and said she did not think another withdrawal was needed, to avoid the commission going into the red as it once did.
The commission has funds available under its existing capital article funding, so the added transfer was judged unnecessary.
Perpetual care interest is available as a backup source, with the principal untouchable and interest earned each year.
Amounts were authorized for the apron, lights and flower plantings, and the unspent portion remains a liability against available funds.
A design price was recalled as roughly forty-something thousand plus a contingency; the initial survey is already paid.
The DPW director had requested repaving all roads, but the interim town manager suggested crack sealing and patching instead.
A resident listed past expenditures and said the commission has funds at its disposal but is asking capital planning for more.

what_happened.line: The Cemetery Commission voted to pull its warrant article for an additional transfer from the sale of lots account.
The commission voted to move forward on the North Cemetery expansion, with capital planning to fund an amount still to be determined.
The commission voted to accept that capital planning will move forward with North Cemetery road repairs; the amount was not settled and the item was not on the latest capital list.
A resident criticised the commission's spending during public comment, said he had submitted a warrant article to rein in its funds, and proposed moving it under the Conservation Commission.
The DPW director is to try to report a count of remaining open plots by the next meeting, set for March 27th.

why_it_matters: The cemetery's expansion and road repairs are now routed through the town's capital plan, so they compete with other capital requests and may reach residents as a Town Meeting vote rather than being paid from the commission's own accounts.

The commission's sale-of-lots account and perpetual care interest are its own funds, and the minutes show a resident-submitted warrant article that would limit them, which residents may be asked to vote on.
